reviews.text: In every example where resolution or a character epiphany occurs, you can point to how Gerwig undercuts those moments in ways that less honest, conventional movies would.
reviews.author: Adam Kempenaar

reviews.text: Saoirse Ronan and Laurie Metcalf are a dynamic duo that will stick with me for a long time. Gerwig’s direction is astounding for a first-timer in how she demonstrates precision and control...
reviews.author: JD Duran

reviews.text: Greta Gerwig is on fire—if her filmography isn’t proof enough of her seemingly limitless talent, “Lady Bird” will be.
reviews.author: Ankit Ojha

reviews.text: Her comedic timing that makes Lady Bird one of the most earnest coming-of-age films of our time, and also one of the funniest...
reviews.author: Brendan Cassidy

reviews.text: Lady Bird is one of the best, realest explorations of the mother daughter relationship ever put to screen.
reviews.author: Rebecca Johnson

reviews.text: Gerwig’s debut is one that will always be relevant, no matter the year. Music will change, fashion will change, but the feelings that Gerwig captures will be forever.
reviews.author: Tina Kakadelis

reviews.text: The warmth, hilarity and at times confronting revelations of teenagehood flood through Gerwig's singular lens.
reviews.author: Jennifer Bisset

reviews.text: Its 2002 post-911 setting feels relevant, its portrait of adolescence feels genuine and personal, and its pitch-perfect and bittersweet final shot lands just right.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: Gerwig bows a modest, spirited film of idiosyncratic dialogue, mannered style, and sharp insight, providing an incredible showcase for the talents of Ronan and Metcalf, as well as her own.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: Greta Gerwig is a major talent.
reviews.author: Fletcher Powell

reviews.text: Though Lady Bird is a coming-of-age story with familiar tropes such as prom night and a disappointing first sexual experience, it's really a film about teenage aspiration.
reviews.author: Nick Levine

reviews.text: Saoirse Ronan's stunning portrayal of adolescence is completely lacking in vanity.
reviews.author: Yasmin Omar

reviews.text: There are many films that try to remind older audience members how it feels to be young, albeit in a superficial way. It reminds us of the real struggles of adolescence while at the same time providing great insight into the challenges of parents...
reviews.author: Ian Brill

reviews.text: Not only incredibly authentic - perhaps cringingly so - but also marginally profound, even as its scope stays strictly on the almost unsubstantial life of a teenager.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: Lady Bird flies high on heartwarming yet tough honesty.
reviews.author: Dan Buffa

reviews.text: With Lady Bird, Greta Gerwig manages to take the old coming-of-age genre and make it feel refreshing with its authenticity and heart.
reviews.author: Matthew St. Clair

reviews.text: Greta Gerwig nails her solo directorial debut in this semi-autobiographical coming-of-age tale where Saoirse Ronan and Laurie Metcalf's mother-daughter scenes bleed with authenticity.
reviews.author: Jason Fraley

reviews.text: [It's] brought to fruition by a wonderful cast . . . namely Ronan and Metcalf, whose push-pull dynamic of blossoming and established worldviews encapsulate the insecurities of growing up.
reviews.author: Matt Cipolla

reviews.text: Being witness to Lady Bird's growth is a beautiful experience. Not only are you enchanted by her story, but you also learn something about yourself. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ricardo Gallegos

reviews.text: There is something for all ages to identify with and you will find yourself torn between the generations, but ultimately feeling great affection for all of the characters. This film is a success because of the exceptional writing from Greta Gerwig.
reviews.author: Fiona Underhill

reviews.text: [The film] is good, but overrated. Curiously, its faults are also overrated, in that many are characteristic of its genre.
reviews.author: CJ Sheu

reviews.text: The way Gerwig captures the stages of adolescence makes this coming-of-age film more honest than poignant. It shows that not only she is a good actress, but also a great filmmaker. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: Marion and Lady Bird's bond is very real, strong, and complicated like many mother-daughter bonds tend to be.
reviews.author: Andrea Thompson

reviews.text: Gerwig shows no hesitation over putting her character in unflattering situations. The laughs come hard, they come often, and they come from all directions.
reviews.author: Victor Stiff

reviews.text: A stupendously acted and immeasurably poignant ode to the realistic bonds and barbs of life as a high school senior.
reviews.author: PJ Nabarro

reviews.text: I am awfully fond of it. This film isn't for me, but it doesn't have to be. Someone out there is going to see this film for the first time. Its heartfelt, goofy, and ever-so-slightly twee wavelength will seem to be made just for them...
reviews.author: Tim Brennan

reviews.text: Oscar-worthy performances, outstanding direction, great script (so real, raw and emotional) along with tremendous editing...
reviews.author: Sarah Knight Adamson

reviews.text: Gerwig deftly mines the family dynamics for laughs and emotion, sometimes in the same scene.
reviews.author: Chris McCoy

reviews.text: Taking the trip with [Lady Bird] is a joy, and the cast and filmmaker taking us there create a singular, authentic experience that will place Lady Bird on the list of most memorable, enjoyable coming of age films.
reviews.author: Leslie Combemale

reviews.text: Lady Bird is a generous portrait from a writer/director/actress who knows something about authenticity.
reviews.author: Nicholas Bell

reviews.text: ... just like Lady Bird, Greta Gerwig is a creative force to be reckoned with.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: Writer/Director Greta Gerwig brings her own personal story into play, delivering her Lady Bird with an enthusiastic yet defiant cheekiness, never once losing sight of the real story.
reviews.author: Kate Rodger

reviews.text: [Greta] Gerwig captures the feeling of being a high schooler so perfectly that it's nearly impossible to not identify with one of the characters in some way.
reviews.author: Karl Delossantos

reviews.text: Gerwig hits the nail on the head for her first solo directorial project.
reviews.author: Allison Rose

reviews.text: Never has the tug of war mother-daughter relationship been so brutally honest on film.
reviews.author: Sara Clements

reviews.text: As irregular and imperfect as any debut of someone who has something valuable to tell. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Loser

reviews.text: One of the best films of the year. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Víctor López G.

reviews.text: Forget the insane hype and you may have a better experience with it. Gerwig's script is gentle and accessible, but also lacks the surprises of a Lena Dunham (Girls) screenplay, the sass of what Diablo Cody (Juno) might have brought to things...
reviews.author: Amelia Harvey

reviews.text: Coming-of-age movies can often feel as ubiquitous as superhero films, yet Lady Bird turns out to be one of those special efforts that manages to leapfrog over the competition with a single bound.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: It's 2002 and 17-year-old Christine "Lady Bird" McPherson is interred in a Catholic high school in California while dreaming resentfully of the East Coast college she's convinced she deserves.
reviews.author: Andiee Paviour

reviews.text: Greta Gerwig's movie flies with humor and universal, high school truths.
reviews.author: Jeff Mitchell

reviews.text: Lady Bird exposes the intoxication with the hallucinatory cocktail of hormones processed by a brain without the experience to sort them.
reviews.author: Ryan Syrek

reviews.text: A beautifully performed and smartly written coming-of-age comedy that displays an astonishing mastery of craft and character.
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: With the latest star-making performance from Saoirse Ronan, Lady Bird is charming and clever and goofy and touching and honest and incredible.
reviews.author: Lisa Trifone

reviews.text: It leans into the complications, the conflicts, the counterintuitive characteristics of growing up, and it's that willingness to allow for paradoxes that establishes its excellence.
reviews.author: Andrew Kendall

reviews.text: Lady Bird takes the tired genre of the coming-of-age story and presents it with an awesome script, real heart, fantastic performances, and honesty.
reviews.author: Kaitlyn Booth

reviews.text: This is just a delightful movie.
reviews.author: Dan Murrell

reviews.text: An achingly relatable relationship between mother and daughter, courtesy of first-time director Greta Gerwig, who knows a thing or two about angst-riddled female characters.
reviews.author: Julie Crawford

reviews.text: The only reason we can relate to it is because of Ronan and Metcalf's brilliant performances.
reviews.author: S. Indra Sathiabalan

reviews.text: This subtle and perceptive coming-of-age film announces Gerwig as a fully-fledged director whose career, I suspect, will be well worth following.
reviews.author: Rachael Mead

reviews.text: It's very well done and feels authentic and natural.
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: Even though some of the jokes are rather obvious, Lady Bird is hugely funny from start to finish, witty writing and sharp sight gags earning the steady stream of laughs one would expect from Gerwig.
reviews.author: Jack Blackwell

reviews.text: Lady Bird is funny and poignant for all the right reasons. It's a simple story without cinematic flourish but plenty of heart.
reviews.author: Deborah Cornelious

reviews.text: It is here the film really shines, throwing a spotlight on a relationship that is so often complicated, and one that female audiences will find completely relatable.
reviews.author: Paula Fleri-Soler

reviews.text: Writer/director Greta Gerwig announces her presence with authority on this one, crafting a remarkable semi-autobiographical portrait of growing up that precisely captures a moment in time.
reviews.author: Allen Adams

reviews.text: The relationship between mothers and daughters is what's at the heart of Lady Bird, and while cringe-worthy at times, it's a beautiful, poignant story that resonated with me.
reviews.author: Amanda Greever

reviews.text: The characters are meaningful and fascinating, the narrative is no slouch, and the story, incredibly simple, is grandiose in terms of gracefulness and spirit.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: Lady Bird is a film that describes the joys, mistakes and dramas of teenage years more eloquently than anything you might see this year.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: The performances are terrific, the dialogue whip-smart, but on a personal level this film didn't grab me. Maybe it's my age, a point when one stops identifying with the irritating daughter and starts nodding along sagely with the irritating mum instead.
reviews.author: Sarah Cartland

reviews.text: There are plenty of moments in a teenage girl's life where the trivial becomes momentous, and they are presented here with a poignant and compassionate vibrancy.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: Gerwig's film isn't quirky for the sake of quirks; she connects her themes of family, faith, and freedom into a wheel of curiosity that allows you to travel along and gain a unique perspective...
reviews.author: James Clay

reviews.text: There's an intuitiveness to Gerwig's masterful screenplay that, in its own way, feels quietly profound, every bit as relatable on this side of the pond as it will be to those who grew up in the boring Sacramento suburbs.
reviews.author: Alistair Ryder

reviews.text: Greta Gerwig, in her first time out of the gate, establishes herself as a confident and intuitive 21st century American filmmaker.
reviews.author: Di Golding

reviews.text: This film champions women, displaying the full range of complicated emotions, untold strengths, and everyday triumphs that are often afforded only men in feature films.
reviews.author: Li Lai

reviews.text: The film still manages to be comedic and natural and leaves you with a sense of empathy for Lady Bird, as we all were her age, with our own problems, not very long ago.
reviews.author: Pooja Pande

reviews.text: You'd be hard-pressed to find more vivid, authentic female characters than in Lady Bird... Be sure not to miss out on one of the decade's ten best movies.
reviews.author: Matt Ward

reviews.text: Strikes a balance between the mumblecore sensibilities of frequent collaborators Joe Swanberg and Noah Baumbach while bringing a refreshingly anarchical female voice into the choir.
reviews.author: Matt Oakes

reviews.text: We already knew that Greta Gerwig was already immensely talented, but Lady Bird just goes to show that she hasn't presented the full extent of her talents until now and Gerwig will be a major force in filmmaking for years to come.
reviews.author: Sean Mulvihill

reviews.text: It all comes back to Ronan and Metcalf, who create a mother-daughter relationship onscreen that is as memorable as any in recent memory.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: It's sincere without ever feeling contrite, intelligent without ever being condescending, and familiar but somehow entirely fresh and unique.
reviews.author: Doug Jamieson

reviews.text: I've loved Greta Gerwig since I first saw her in "Hannah Takes the Stairs" and I'm ecstatic to report that her first feature film 100% lives up to the hype.
reviews.author: Lindsay Pugh

reviews.text: Everything about it is a true delight.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: Lady Bird tells a familiar narrative, but its lead has, rather brilliantly, managed to package it with freshness that entertains and prompts reflection.
reviews.author: Nguyên Lê

reviews.text: At another time, on a second or third or fourth watch, I'm sure I will be able to find something to criticize about Lady Bird. But right now, having ruminated on this film for a full day, there is little to nitpick.
reviews.author: Lauren Humphries-Brooks

reviews.text: While Greta Gerwig may have painted her wings, it is the boldly captivating and nuanced performance from Saoirse Ronan that ultimately allows Lady Bird to fly.
reviews.author: Aaron Peterson

reviews.text: This is a enjoyable and refreshing drama which is definitely a must see on its road to wide-release. Go see it... then go call your mom.
reviews.author: Kimberly Pierce

reviews.text: It feels real because the writing doesn't shy away from the pain and awkwardness and unexpected joys of the life it depicts.
reviews.author: Ross Miller

reviews.text: Lady Bird combines wisdom and tenderness, humor and grace. It's light-footed without being lightweight. And it captures, with great feeling, the turbulence of a girl growing up. I can't recommend it enough.
reviews.author: Anupama Chopra

reviews.text: Greta Gerwig's directorial debut, Lady Bird, is the millisecond of possibility, the speck of unflinching nerve, which might only occur once in our lives.
reviews.author: Robert Daniels

reviews.text: Delivered with masterful direction and a script that relates to the teenager in all of us.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: Exquisitely renders the complex, funny, turbulent love between mother and daughter, which is to say, the way desire can feel like betrayal.
reviews.author: Amanda Jane Robinson

reviews.text: Gerwig and her cast and crew make Lady Bird look so easy that you might initially write it off as charming and slight - but this cinematic yearbook of a confident, flawed girl making her way into the world under her own power is big and vital and true.
reviews.author: Molly Templeton

reviews.text: I can't wait to see what Gerwig does next.
reviews.author: Amelie Lasker

reviews.text: Experiences like Lady Bird are few and far between, especially so from a first-time director. A true testament to what cinema is capable of.
reviews.author: Millicent Thomas

reviews.text: Lady Bird is Gerwig's second feature and shows a great deal of talent. She also wrote the film, and... [it] feels very personal and intimate. Her writing feels genuine, the words natural, and gives the movie a very real energy.
reviews.author: Kat Hughes

reviews.text: Hopeful and true, Lady Bird remains comfortable in its own skin even as it confronts the seemingly endless anxieties of young people in transition.
reviews.author: Glenn Heath Jr.

reviews.text: Lady Bird, is in its own movie making lane, and does it all without missing anything.
reviews.author: Leah Sydney

reviews.text: Saoirse Ronan is not only finest working actor of her generation, but she elevates everything she's in. With all the things going for this movie, it makes it even better.
reviews.author: Wesley Lovell

reviews.text: It is a female coming-of-age story that is both nostalgic and unflinching, and it will ensnare you deeply in its grasp.
reviews.author: Roxana Hadadi

reviews.text: An endearing film experience that's profoundly captivating. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos Díaz Reyes

reviews.text: The story speckled with humor and emotionally charged moments is the perfect coming of age story for the everyday woman.
reviews.author: Ashley Menzel

reviews.text: There are certain films that strike a personal chord, and Lady Bird is one of those despite the fact that I am both male and Canadian and this is set in Sacramento featuring Saoirse Ronan as the lead.
reviews.author: Jason Wilson

reviews.text: There's a mixture of sentimental lightness and the strong contradictions of an unmanageable age that create a substantial, valuable film. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: William Venegas

reviews.text: The sweet, charming "Lady Bird" is a love letter to the cinema of ambitious adolescents.
reviews.author: David Keyes

reviews.text: Lady Bird is stunning in its precision, in its consistent ability to spark the most penetrating of emotions out of scenes that seem ordinary and routine.
reviews.author: Oggs Cruz

reviews.text: [Greta] Gerwig's ability with actors is one of her most striking achievements, and she draws out incredible nuance from her own carefully woven script - full of tonal U-turns and emotional syncopations.
reviews.author: Jason Di Rosso

reviews.text: Greta Gerwig's Lady Bird is populated by actors who, like Gerwig herself, can do no wrong. That enhances the film's goody-goody quality, which falls over the movie like a warm blanket.
reviews.author: A.S. Hamrah

reviews.text: The charm of Lady Bird is not its use of cinematographic language...but it's exciting in its portrayal of adolescence and the construction of identity. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Aloma Rodríguez

reviews.text: What separates Lady Bird from the pack is the funny, heartfelt way in delves into the relationship between mother and daughter.
reviews.author: Matthew Toomey

reviews.text: Lady Bird might just be the new classic of the comic of age story.
reviews.author: Amelia Navascues

reviews.text: Lady Bird is a labor of love from [Greta Gerwig]. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Benjamín Harguindey

reviews.text: This is gorgeously balanced portraiture that can laugh at its precocious heroine with much affection while tracing her formative journey with the dignity it deserves.
reviews.author: Hilary A White

reviews.text: A wry and often understated movie about identity and aspiration that manages to feel fresh, despite familiar beats.
reviews.author: Ed Whitfield

reviews.text: One factor that makes Lady Bird special is the excellent structuring of the narrative arcs. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: Gerwig's writing prowess shines through: the dialogue is butter-smooth and manages to sound clever yet not contrived...Gerwig seems to take delight in overturning cliches. Her directorial debut brims with emotion and talent.
reviews.author: Soumya Rao

reviews.text: Lady Bird is one of the most affecting coming-of-age movies in recent memory.
reviews.author: Rashid Irani

reviews.text: Saoirse Ronan, 23, has three Oscar nominations already. What have you been doing with your life?
reviews.author: Rohan Naahar

reviews.text: Lady Bird, above all, wants to be part of something big. And now she is -- she's the sensational lead character in one of the most winning, witty and wise films of the year.
reviews.author: Roe McDermott

reviews.text: Just like the protagonist, Lady Bird is awkwardly funny yet bittersweet, making it one of Hollywood's most original and refreshingly honest films about growing up.
reviews.author: Neil Soans

reviews.text: It's a film that is enjoyed from its commencement. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: Actress turned writer-director Greta Gerwig has turned out a funny, engaging picture driven by the twin poles of Christine and Marion (Metcalf).
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: ...a solid debut from a promising new filmmaker.
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: Lady Bird uses its eponymous protagonist in the construction of one of the most skeptical voices of modern cinematography. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alberto Sáez Villarino

reviews.text: There is no doubt that it has a certain charm. I guess a lot of its appeal lies in its accessibility, its slightly subversive attitude and its hipster aura. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jaime Fa de Lucas

reviews.text: Gerwig's film, which closes with a tribute to Sacramento, ends well and feels sincere. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Hugo Hernández Valdivia

reviews.text: ...beautiful, delicate and precise. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Luis Martínez

reviews.text: A pleasant and fresh surprise, it reminds me a bit of Juno. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Israel Acosta Aroche

reviews.text: ...nice and warm. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fernanda Solórzano

reviews.text: [Greta] Gerwig manages to narrate a common experience without falling into the clichés of Hollywood. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: María Fernanda Mugica

reviews.text: ...refined, balanced and precise. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jordi Costa

reviews.text: The meanest thing we could say about Greta Gerwig's Lady Bird is that there isn't enough of it. Maybe we're being greedy. Maybe 93 minutes is the perfect running time. That way, we can be sure we'll never tire of repeat viewings.
reviews.author: Chris Wasser

reviews.text: Lady Bird is a charming, graceful and humorous story about growing up in a small town.
reviews.author: Ben Sin

reviews.text: By the time the film wraps up, you'll be filled with a lot of emotion, ranging from nostalgia to relief. Lady Bird is relatable, honest, doesn't take itself seriously and features some charming shots of Sacramento.
reviews.author: Masego Panyane

reviews.text: Lady Bird is a teen movie written by someone who remembers what it was like to be a teen, and one that understands that a character can be difficult without being irredeemable.
reviews.author: Alex Doenau

reviews.text: Saoirse Ronan turns in her best performance yet in this delightful feel good drama with some very sharp edges.
reviews.author: Alan Corr

reviews.text: It tells a personal story - which is also full of universal themes - in its own way, which differentiates it from other coming of age stories. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: As played by Saoirse Ronan, Lady Bird is a mixed bag of emotions - hurtling between delight, sorrow, fear and anger, full of abrupt, capricious energy.
reviews.author: Michael Bonner

reviews.text: A coming of age film for grown-ups, I recommend Lady Bird wholeheartedly.
reviews.author: Aoife O'Ceallachain

reviews.text: ...an unexpectedly tender coming of age piece.
reviews.author: Luke Goodsell

reviews.text: The densely packed detail which makes this such a luminous work shows Gerwig to be an uncommonly alert filmmaker.
reviews.author: Ryan Gilbey

reviews.text: This Irish actress has the ability to turn a simple, straightforward story into something tender, heartwarming and affecting.
reviews.author: Joanne Soh

reviews.text: The naturalistic depiction of relationships is Gerwig's evident strength.
reviews.author: Sarah Watt

reviews.text: Although the film does not shine for its originality, it works in its favor that it is not killing itself to be. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Phillipp Engel

reviews.text: One of the finest teen comedies ever. Movie perfection
reviews.author: Larushka Ivan-Zadeh

reviews.text: Lady Bird is an absolute sunrise of a movie, the kind of thing that makes your heart leap and gives you hope, brings you as much joy as your best friend's wedding, and makes people like me write over elaborate opening sentences to praise it.
reviews.author: Jonathan Dean

reviews.text: One element of the film's genius is its ability to root us firmly in Lady Bird's perspective. It does more.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: Gerwig's future career behind the camera is off to a superb start. Though Lady Bird perhaps lacks that genuine streak of eye-catching innovation, what it does it does extremely well.
reviews.author: Daniel Green

reviews.text: The story of Lady Bird is accessible to all viewers, perhaps more inclined to the female eye, but one way or another all experience this journey to maturity. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Adrián Ruiz

reviews.text: I highly recommend this film, especially if you are a teenager or you have teenage children or if you were a teenager. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: David Ocadiz

reviews.text: Lady Bird translates into cinema the crystalline and profound prose of Joan Didion. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Andrea G. Bermejo

reviews.text: An entertaining, honest and well-achieved film. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jonathan Sánchez

reviews.text: This film has achieved some notoriety for the cultural climate that Hollywood is experiencing at this time. If Hollywood wanted to nominate a woman, they could name Eliza Hittman or Kathryn Bigelow. (Full Review in Reforma newspaper, in Spanish).
reviews.author: Ernesto Diezmartinez

reviews.text: Restraint ... gives the film its credibility and charm.
reviews.author: Andy Lea

reviews.text: Its joyful, forward-rushing narrative rhythm captures the feeling of adolescence ending before it has barely begun.
reviews.author: Simran Hans

reviews.text: Unusually perceptive when it comes to matters of class and money, Lady Bird finds its dramatic heart in their testy, affectionate relationship, the most indelibly drawn mother and daughter since Terms of Endearment.
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: The film is not so much a coming-of-age story...[it] aims for a deeper truth, being that life's most important lessons come incrementally, in small, touching moments, something Lady Bird comes to appreciate, however reluctantly.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: This is strongly-acted throughout but really held together by Ronan.
reviews.author: David 'Mad Dog' Bradley

reviews.text: Not ground-breaking territory, but, as one of the kindly nuns tells [Lady bird], love is all about paying attention.
reviews.author: Markie Robson-Scott

reviews.text: The fact that it is in so many senses ordinary, although it rebels against its mediocrity, is what makes Lady Bird work above other films about teenagers. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Daniel Krauze

reviews.text: Lady Bird's depiction of the intense and difficult relationship between a commonsense mother and her whimsical daughter is pitch perfect in its mix of love, disappointment and resentment.
reviews.author: Rochelle Siemienowicz

reviews.text: As teen movies go, it's supremely sophisticated, capturing and crystallising that moment in adolescence when it seems that life is at last about to start and the only place you want to be is elsewhere.
reviews.author: Sandra Hall

reviews.text: An intimate display of such a deep and true relationship between a mother and her daughter. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Arturo Magaña

reviews.text: Goes without saying this is already a lock for one of the best movies of 2018.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: While there is an acute authorial intelligence informing the transitions between scenes, the steady trot of clipped vignettes comes to seem monotonous and somewhat evasive, a way to move along before anything too hard and hurtful happens.
reviews.author: Nick Pinkerton

reviews.text: Like many wonderful actresses with a gift for words (think Julie Delpy, Sarah Polley and Lake Bell) Gerwig has slipped behind the camera to create something quietly political.
reviews.author: Charlotte O'Sullivan

reviews.text: A terrific, joyous film.
reviews.author: Jamie East

reviews.text: It's remarkable how heartfelt each and every moment feels, without the film once descending into sentimentality.
reviews.author: Emma Simmonds

reviews.text: Lady Bird could still become bogged down in the dreary familiarity of its setting were it not for a sharp script by Gerwig and a terrifically likeable lead performance by Ronan.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: Gerwig's deft handling of script, camera and actors is all the more impressive given that this is her first film as solo director.
reviews.author: Ed Potton

reviews.text: Just like its title character, Lady Bird is quirky and sentimental but despite best attempts, never really defines itself into anything meaningful.
reviews.author: Alachia Queen

reviews.text: This is a coming-of-age story that's affecting without ever being sentimental, and feels absolutely true -- like remembering the teenager you once were, even if you were never a Lady Bird (or Debee) exactly. A rare bird indeed.
reviews.author: Deborah Ross

reviews.text: The results borrow freely from French New Wave, American teen drama, and more - but the great triumph of Lady Bird is that it remains in Gerwig's voice: it's fresh, funny, and lastingly poignant.
reviews.author: Edward Lawrenson

reviews.text: It is both painfully honest and laugh-out-loud funny at the same time.
reviews.author: Matthew Turner

reviews.text: A gloriously funny and wistfully autobiographical coming-of-age comedy.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: If Gerwig is capable of all this in her first solo feature, who knows what feats of woodwork she'll craft for us next.
reviews.author: Tim Robey

reviews.text: First time writer-director Greta Gerwig, an experienced actor, is attuned to the mix of munificence and selfishness that makes up the adolescent heart.
reviews.author: Anwen Crawford

reviews.text: Writer-director Gerwig manages brilliantly the delicate feat of portraying the vulnerabilities and eccentricities of the townsfolk without patronising them.
reviews.author: Geoffrey Macnab

reviews.text: The script is fantastic - smart, witty, revealing, precise, and concise ... Ronan is staggeringly charming and appealing, even when Lady Bird is not ... I could have watched it for days.
reviews.author: CJ Johnson

reviews.text: Lady Bird is an absolute charmer of a movie. We genuinely care about this lovely, rebellious girl and we want her to be happy.
reviews.author: David Stratton

reviews.text: It's almost too hard to write about Lady Bird precisely because it's so brilliant that no words could possibly capture its spirit and convey why this film absolutely has to be seen, and loved.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: Lady Bird is a gem. File this one next to Juno, Edge of Seventeen, and The Way Way Back, and not too far away from your favourite John Hughes movie.
reviews.author: Graeme Tuckett

reviews.text: Lady Bird... feels like a watershed moment for female audiences in general, offering mothers a working, warts-and-all screen version of themselves that they actually recognise.
reviews.author: Vicky Roach

reviews.text: Gerwig may well have just directed a film better than any one she's starred in - and her back catalogue is hardly poor.
reviews.author: Stefan Pape

reviews.text: Smart, funny and emotional, Lady Bird is a Trojan horse movie - sneaking its way into hearts and minds via well-worn tropes.
reviews.author: Jane Crowther

reviews.text: A coming-of-age story like no other, Lady Bird is smart, emotional, funny and completely original. Rarely has a directorial debut been so assured, so singular and so heartwarmingly affecting.
reviews.author: Terri White

reviews.text: Almost everything here bespeaks Gerwig, including the cast's tendency to act one line or dramatic moment with breezy brio, as if already on the run to the next. Very GG.
reviews.author: Nigel Andrews

reviews.text: Gerwig's film moves beyond a traditional coming-of-age 'lessons learned' conclusion, into rather a moving portrait of the intimate ties we have with place.
reviews.author: Patrick Gamble

reviews.text: Lady Bird asks the cinematic question, "How baller can one movie be?" And then it answers it emphatically: "Very baller."
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: Beautiful coming of age story.
reviews.author: Steph Cozza

reviews.text: evokes a shared sense of adolescent turmoil that is neither melodramatic nor condescending, but rather perfectly pitched at a recognizable human level that allows virtually anyone to identify and empathize with the travails of its protagonist
reviews.author: James Kendrick

reviews.text: Its brushstrokes are light, and it never overextends - or extends, really. Its energies are almost wholly inward-directed.
reviews.author: Rob Gonsalves

reviews.text: It is an unfortunate game in which a film seeks its identity while chasing a ghostly character who in turn seeks her own personality. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: Laurie Metcalf steals the film from Saoirse Ronan, in a subtle piece of acting so raw and genuine it hurts. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mario Alegre

reviews.text: Charming, funny and authentic, 'Lady Bird' is an impressive outing by Greta Gerwig in the director's chair. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: There is something sweet and quirky about Greta Gerwig's semi-autobiographical coming of age story, Lady Bird. It has a lovely lilt about it: an effortless flow of character-driven action that amuses and endears.
reviews.author: Louise Keller

reviews.text: With writing and direction this smart, Lady Bird is a joy to watch.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: One of the most delicate and intelligent films of 2017. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alejandro G. Calvo

reviews.text: A really honest, real depiction of what it's like growing up.
reviews.author: Kristian Harloff

reviews.text: Saoirse Ronan is a threat to win a statue everytime she's on screen and her performance in [Lady Bird] is just another step.
reviews.author: Mark Ellis

reviews.text: ... Lady Bird is a great entry in what's a tricky genre...
reviews.author: James Bartlett

reviews.text: Specific yet always relatable, Gerwig stitches it all together like she's borrowing from shared memories.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: 'I guess I pay attention,' says Lady Bird, explaining the loving detail found in one of her essays; from the evidence here, Gerwig does, too.
reviews.author: John Beifuss

reviews.text: Lady Bird hits the mark of the American teen movie while quietly reaching toward literary effect [including] a set of sequences of driving in Sacramento [that] fall into place with the weight of a two-story house.
reviews.author: Ray Pride

reviews.text: Saiorse Ronan delivers a stellar performance, with Laurie Metcalf as her put-upon mom, and both will likely score Oscar noms along with this instant-classic movie overall.
reviews.author: Carl Kozlowski

reviews.text: It's that sense that Christine is still a work in progress that makes Lady Bird such an fascinating watch with enough intrigue to make a sequel viable.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Lyles

reviews.text: Gerwig is traveling backwards as a writer from Frances Ha to Mistress America to Lady Bird. That trilogy of films is, dare I say, even better than Francois Truffaut's collected Adventures of Antoine Doinel.
reviews.author: Brian Formo

reviews.text: Gerwig's movie doesn't say much new about growing up cool with parents who aren't. But it says plenty about Gerwig's talent, another channel for a distinctive voice of her generation.
reviews.author: Steve Persall

reviews.text: Metcalf gives a prickly and heartbreaking performance, and she's not the only one supplied with grace notes: Almost every character gets one or another.
reviews.author: Jesse Hassenger

reviews.text: Yet while [Greta] Gerwig doesn't exactly reinvent the coming-of-age genre, she packs it with great scenes, dialogue and performances
reviews.author: Andrew Osborne

reviews.text: For a film that dwells in the past, Gerwig avoids banal sentimentality, instead offering us something excitingly present and ephemeral.
reviews.author: Alejandro Veciana

reviews.text: There are more funny lines in Lady Bird's first five minutes than in most films.
reviews.author: Brian Gibson

reviews.text: Ronan, well on her way to being one of the greatest film actresses of the 21st century, is the movie's second-biggest asset after Gerwig herself, followed closely by Metcalf in perhaps the role of her career.
reviews.author: Jim Lane

reviews.text: A tidy 90 minutes that I wanted never to end.
reviews.author: Al Hoff

reviews.text: It's easily one of the freshest, sharpest and most enjoyable films of this year.
reviews.author: Loren King

reviews.text: 'Lady Bird' is as edgy and funny as growing up.
reviews.author: Linda Cook

reviews.text: Lady Bird is a brilliant little movie that deals with ideas both big and small. But, most powerful is the relationship between Lady Bird and Marion. It is harsh and funny and sometimes hard to watch. But it is undeniably and eternally there.
reviews.author: Alexandra MacAaron

reviews.text: Though Gerwig's talents as a writer-director shine, it's the casting of Ronan in the lead that makes "Lady Bird" such a memorable work. The layers she gives the character will make the performance go down as one of the best high school characters ever.
reviews.author: Jason Guerrasio

reviews.text: LADY BIRD is a KAREN, a racist, homophobic, dishonest, and disloyal character that Hollywood & the media profited from while attempting to silence me.
reviews.author: Cole Smithey

reviews.text: The acting in this movie is really good, especially by Laurie Metcalf, who gives an exceptional performance. It is the film's political metaphor, however, that really lifts it above the standard coming of age movie.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: ... taps into passion and fear on the edge of innocence.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: A fantastic, female-centric, instant classic reminiscent of both Juno (2007) and Bridesmaids (2011).
reviews.author: Kam Williams

reviews.text: This is a coming-of-age story like no other thanks to the insightful writing and brisk directorial style of Gerwig, who makes Lady Bird's story a consistently surprising one.
reviews.author: Bob Grimm

reviews.text: If you can't relate to this movie, you probably somehow went from childhood right into adulthood, completely skipping over adolescence.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: A charming but mild comedy defined by a nice performance from Laurie Metcalf as Lady Bird's mother Marion and a handful of appreciably relatable millennial moments.
reviews.author: J. Olson

reviews.text: It's all relatable and arresting to watch unfold, with a heartwarming closing shot that will make you want to call your Mama and tell her you love her
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: For all we know, an authentic look at high-school life focusing on the myriad talents of Saoirse Ronan (her first name rhymes with "inertia").
reviews.author: Harvey S. Karten

reviews.text: Saoirse Ronan is one of the brightest stars of her generation, able to switch from ebullient to tormented, confident to awkward in an instant and never uttering a false note.
reviews.author: Brooke Corso

reviews.text: A completely pleasant movie, in a low-stakes, low-key way.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: Ronan's chemistry with her castmates is always first rate, but her work here with Metcalf is particularly sharp.
reviews.author: Piers Marchant

reviews.text: There's nothing new story-wise where Greta Gerwig's directorial debut "Lady Bird" is concerned, yet the magic of the film is that somehow it seems that we are seeing it, if not for the first time, with a sense of discovery.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: The characters may be messy, but Gerwig's writing and direction are elegantly precise. One of the best ensemble casts of the year.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: First-time director Greta Gerwig has created a film that's heartfelt, sometimes heartbreaking and a sure Oscar contender.
reviews.author: Tim Appelo

reviews.text: The key to Lady Bird is that Marion is never painted as an ogre. Her toughness is played for comic effect: as an understandable character flaw born of her genuinely meaning well.
reviews.author: Noel Murray

reviews.text: Gerwig finds a warmer part of herself when, unencumbered by any lab partner, she returns to her hometown with Lady Bird. One can only hope that, this time, she stays.
reviews.author: J. R. Jones

reviews.text: A dramedy that will appeal to all women who have experienced large doses of love and pain in their relationships with difficult mothers.
reviews.author: Frederic and Mary Ann Brussat

reviews.text: A heartfelt coming-of-age story that perfectly captures the bittersweet transition from adolescence to dawning adulthood...
reviews.author: April Wolfe

reviews.text: While Gerwig has assembled an extraordinary ensemble cast. Ronan has to rate as first among equals.
reviews.author: Eleanor Ringel Cater

reviews.text: Saoirse Ronan gives a standout, brilliant performance and so does Laurie Metcalf as her long-suffering, big-hearted mother. It's a remarkable solo directorial debut from Greta Gerwig.
reviews.author: William Bibbiani

reviews.text: Just as carefreeness requires effort, so "growing up" never ends.
reviews.author: Margot Harrison

reviews.text: Lady Bird's unvarnished, unglamorized high-school drama has the quirky humor one expects from Gerwig...Ultimately, it's a mother-daughter love story, replete with the tribulations of painful individuation.
reviews.author: Peter Canavese

reviews.text: A specific story with universal, emotional resonance, Lady Bird shows us the fruits of paying attention.
reviews.author: Meghan Gilligan

reviews.text: ...a deeply funny film that still manages to grapple with some heady emotional territory.
reviews.author: Travis Johnson

reviews.text: Lady Bird may fall short of being one of the all-time great high school movies, but Saoirse Ronan makes it enthralling at all times.
reviews.author: Kristian M. Lin

reviews.text: This is a gorgeous movie made by a gorgeous spirit.
reviews.author: Drew McWeeny

reviews.text: The affection with which she portrays her hometown on screen, coupled with the impatience of her youthful alter-ego, imbues much of Lady Bird with a refreshing ring of truth.
reviews.author: Lisa Jensen

reviews.text: The message of Gerwig's Lady Bird changes depending on which side of motherhood you sit.
reviews.author: Kathryn Lindsay

reviews.text: What Gerwig has done is skillfully create a world where her characters can fully develop.
reviews.author: Dan Webster

reviews.text: Greta Gerwig's official directorial debut will make you laugh and then steal your heart.
reviews.author: Matt Hoffman

reviews.text: The movie is wonderful and true, an act of love in all its contradictions and complexity.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: Greta Gerwig has crafted an effectively empathetic coming-of-age story, filled with sassy, bittersweet anguish.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: Greta Gerwig makes a winning directorial debut with a funny and very human comedy that happens to have Oscar-caliber performances from Saoirse Ronan and Laurie Metcalf.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: [A] hysterical love letter to home, high school, and the history of ourselves.
reviews.author: Matt Patches

reviews.text: This is our story, as comfortable as an old pair of worn-out leather slippers. Step in and relive your own personal journey.
reviews.author: Frank Wilkins

reviews.text: We are doomed to like this movie.
reviews.author: Molly Laich

reviews.text: Lady Bird is smoothly tender and will speak to everyone everywhere, in unexpectedly sweet and cutely funny ways, if you give it a chance to do so - which I hope you do.
reviews.author: Bill Arceneaux

reviews.text: "Lady Bird" is such a beautiful, genuine creation, launching Gerwig's directorial career on a blindingly bright note, promising sharp, searching humanist efforts to come.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: What's remarkable about the film is that it takes a story and related subject matter that we've seen countless times before and makes it all feels fresh and interesting. (Full Content Review for Parents - Profanity, Sex, etc. - also Available)
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: It's rare to see a relationship between two complicated women portrayed with such care and empathy.
reviews.author: Shannon Gormley

reviews.text: Between Ronan's performance, Gerwig's wit and a story that finishes in a place that feels more satisfying than you might expect, Lady Bird adds up to a journey that encounters plenty of potholes but arrives intact.
reviews.author: Josh Terry

reviews.text: Lady Bird is an enjoyable film, with a honest heart about it.
reviews.author: Mike Reyes

reviews.text: Lady Bird makes for a delightful coming of age comedy/drama, fueled by Gerwig's inspired direction and Saoirse Ronan's charming performance.
reviews.author: Sandy Schaefer

reviews.text: Lady Bird's center is the relationship between Christine and her mother, and Metcalf's performance is a knockout.
reviews.author: Karen Han

reviews.text: Saoirse Ronan... is perfect for the role of the rebellious girl who dreams of more, but does not want to completely destroy the hearts of her parents. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Aurélie Dupire

reviews.text: As she does as an actress, Gerwig the director articulates every delicate, emotional nuance. For a debut feature film, it is a triumph.
reviews.author: Lee Jutton

reviews.text: Lady Bird manages to feel like a lover letter to home without being cloyingly sweet
reviews.author: Megan Moffat

reviews.text: Gerwig packs an impressive amount of relatable teen angst into just 93 minutes, all while maintaining a sharp sense of humor and an authentic voice. There's not an ounce of contrivance.
reviews.author: Eric D. Snider

reviews.text: It produces a rare match made for mother/daughter movie heaven, and Gerwig and her gifted girls just about get us there.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: As much as I love Gerwig's sunny, grounded presence as a screen actor, her assured solo directorial debut demonstrates why we need women to get behind the camera.
reviews.author: Alison Gillmor

reviews.text: Lady Bird, in a year without a clear front-runner, could take flight and usher in the kind of impactful changes in the film industry we've been dreaming of and whispering about for the last decade.
reviews.author: tt stern-enzi

reviews.text: Christine/Lady Bird is easy enough to root for, even when missteps are made.
reviews.author: Gary Rotstein

reviews.text: ... an astute, clever, often funny, and poignant portrait of the teenage transition to adulthood.
reviews.author: Diane Carson

reviews.text: Happily engaging and marked by Ronan's wit and vulnerability, Lady Bird introduces us to a young woman who's taking small and large steps on one of life's more exciting journeys: discovering herself.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: If Gerwig's cinematic brand is going to be tenderness, feminism, spiky humor, and empathy, count me in.
reviews.author: Max Weiss

reviews.text: "Lady Bird" is a wise and funny film about a teenage girl's coming of age. But it's just as wise and funny about being the parents of that teenage girl.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: ...an astonishingly assured first film from Gerwig...
reviews.author: Sarah Boslaugh

reviews.text: The best films of this genre always show a path and provide a takeaway for being a better person. Lady Bird does just that.
reviews.author: Bill Clark

reviews.text: "Lady Bird" is a deeply accomplished debut, as much a love letter to Gerwig's hometown as it is to awkward adolescence. It flies.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: The recent past is a harder sell, given its freshness in living memory, and Greta Gerwig pulls off an even more difficult trick: depicting her own millennial adolescence in the sun-bleached Sacramento Valley of the early aughties.
reviews.author: Ken Eisner

reviews.text: A coming-of-age film that stands head and shoulders above most in that popular genre... smart, incisive and emotionally satisfying,
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: With a delightful lead performance from Ronan and a breezy script built on universal themes, it effortlessly takes wing to become an embraceable exploration of growing up.
reviews.author: Mike Scott

reviews.text: Everyone will be guaranteed some adoration for Lady Bird, who has made all the romantic and social mistakes you expect a young girl to make while ravenous for distinction but has learned from them all on the way to a thoroughly unpredictable womanhood.
reviews.author: Jeff Simon

reviews.text: The good news is that the film doesn't fall off from the standard it sets in opening.
reviews.author: M. Faust

reviews.text: What's most delightful about Lady Bird is that Gerwig brings an unabashedly earnest point of view to Lady Bird's sometimes rocky road to adulthood. The hipster cynicism is gone, and the sincerity shines through.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: We don't have a whole lot of honest, funny and good coming-of-age stories with strong female leads. Lady Bird is timely in that need, but its themes are timeless. It's one of the funniest and best films of the year.
reviews.author: Brad Keefe

reviews.text: Lots of movies are set to be popping up in multiplexes, but few as wonderful as "Lady Bird."
reviews.author: Calvin Wilson

reviews.text: Lady Bird is easily one of the year's best ways to spend your time and money at the movies. It bounces by at 93 minutes and maintains a shoulder-shrugging tone that makes its truths land all the more powerfully.
reviews.author: Stephen Rebello

reviews.text: "Lady Bird" is the kind of indie film like such recent hits "Moonlight" or "Boyhood" that possess mainstream crossover and critical appeal.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: It's also funny, very real and fast-moving.
reviews.author: Diane Pershing

reviews.text: One of the best movies about adolescence to come along in years.
reviews.author: Rafer Guzman

reviews.text: The movie is a coming-of-age tale, but it's also a story of loving, warring mother and daughter at the point of separation, presented by Gerwig with great affection and skill, to hilarious, and moving effect.
reviews.author: Gary Thompson

reviews.text: Lady Bird is only beginning to mature by the time the movie ends, but as a filmmaker, Gerwig proves that she's already there.
reviews.author: Josh Bell

reviews.text: Just when we thought the stale "coming-of-age" film was on a precipitous slide, along comes the most unlikely of lifelines.
reviews.author: Cameron Meier

reviews.text: Lady Bird' is a fresh and sincere feature, a wonderful and compassionate coming-of-age story that is funny, observant and endearing.
reviews.author: Bob Bloom

reviews.text: The ordinary has become special thanks to the vision of these three women.
reviews.author: Laura DeMarco

reviews.text: I'm not sure there's a single unsuccessful moment in this entire film. This was the movie that reminded me how much I can still love a movie.
reviews.author: Vincent Mancini

reviews.text: ... in the writing-directing debut of actress-turned-filmmaker Greta Gerwig, with Ronan and a carefully chosen cast of characters, the time-worn genre twinkles like new.
reviews.author: Kelly Vance

reviews.text: Gerwig's screenplay reflects sincerity and compassion in its depiction of a young woman striving for independence while balancing adolescent obligations.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: Lady Bird will stay with you long after the credits roll, helping it to become one of the definitive coming-of-age movies of our time.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: ... "Lady Bird" is a nearly perfect film-perhaps of the funniest and most endearing coming-of-age film to come along since "Rushmore.
reviews.author: Peter Sobczynski

reviews.text: It's funny, sad, witty, observant and captivating.
reviews.author: Anita Katz

reviews.text: This generous comedy, with its focus on a girl's life, is better than the kind of films they don't make anymore. It's the low-budget, high-incandescence movie we're all told it's impossible to make today.
reviews.author: Richard von Busack

reviews.text: A striking directorial debut by Greta Gerwig, this tender, semi-autobiographical love letter to Gerwig's hometown explores the gulf between childhood and adulthood with touching, witty humor.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: Lady Bird isn't a teen romance. It's the love story between a girl and her mother, who loves so fiercely it's scary.
reviews.author: Annlee Ellingson

reviews.text: ... I love this movie, and it's hard not to believe that general audience who head to the theatre to give it a look will not end up feeling exactly the same.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: Lady Bird understands late adolescence as the endless accumulations of tiny humiliations and a deep, unutterable yearning for escape.
reviews.author: Zach Schonfeld

reviews.text: Lady Bird may sound slight, but it offers an eloquent, fresh voice from a thoroughly accomplished film-maker.
reviews.author: Caryn James

reviews.text: The delightful and insightful Lady Bird achieves flight in its own unique way, just like the aerodynamically unorthodox ladybug the title tips to.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: There's a lot of truth in Gerwig's film ... and there's also a sense of searching for that truth...
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: ...has a genuine love for its characters' foibles, which it rightly regards as clumsy attempts at self-expression.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: Lady Bird is a coming-of-age story distinguished by a great script and a perfect cast.
reviews.author: Liz Braun

reviews.text: Lady Bird will definitely hold your attention.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: This is a small, humorous movie in some ways, but it has a huge heart. What a nice experience.
reviews.author: Charles Ealy

reviews.text: Highlighted by an awards-worthy performance by Saoirse Ronan and structured around a light, witty script by Gerwig, the movie delivers a well-targeted snapshot of a year-in-the-life of an ordinary high school senior.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: It's unique and original and fresh and wonderful, and can you tell I loved it?
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: Saoirse Ronan plays Lady Bird as if she'd been following writer-director Greta Gerwig around all her life - mannerisms and liberated worldview fully internalized.
reviews.author: Bob Mondello

reviews.text: [Saoirse Ronan and Laurie Metcalf's] verbal battles are hilarious, their stalemates wrenching, their tender moments intoxicating.
reviews.author: Sean Nelson

reviews.text: Greta Gerwig proves that she is her own muse
reviews.author: Marjorie Baumgarten

reviews.text: It's a great movie.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: An emotional feast full of humor and pathos about the audacity, the wonder, the horror that is female adolescence. Beautiful, bittersweet, and very generous.
reviews.author: MaryAnn Johanson

reviews.text: As soon as it was over, I wanted to watch it again.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: In Ronan's marvelous performance, tough and transparent at the same time, we can see the blurred outlines of the equally assured filmmaker behind her.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: "Lady Bird" is a triumph of style, sensibility and spirit. The girl at its center may not be a heavyweight, but her movie is epic.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: I love it. If a more enchanted movie comes along this year, I'll be surprised.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: This is simply beautiful work.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: The film soars because it scans as real, each character someone who might very well live next door, struggling with everyday issues - family, sex, love, money, status, expectation, and disappointment.
reviews.author: Kim Hughes

reviews.text: As an actor, Gerwig has shown an enchantingly light touch; she brings that to her work as director, as "Lady Bird" skims along happily, showing us moments both crucial and trivial in a teenage girl's life.
reviews.author: Moira MacDonald

reviews.text: Smartly refreshes the rebellious teen girl movie...in a sympathetic way that could appeal to teens and mothers.
reviews.author: Nora Lee Mandel

reviews.text: Greta Gerwig has reclaimed the narrative around virginity - and it's all the better for it.
reviews.author: Anne Cohen

reviews.text: One of this year's prized films.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: Greta Gerwig's coming-of-age film is deft, joyous, and imaginatively sympathetic
reviews.author: K. Austin Collins

reviews.text: Gerwig's stuffed a lot of story into her 93 minute comedy, yet it never feels overpacked nor have any of her cast been given short shrift, a remarkable achievement.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: Gerwig the actress skillfully pivots between the wacky and the poignant, so it's no surprise that Gerwig the auteur so delicately balances hilarity and heartbreak.
reviews.author: Alonso Duralde

reviews.text: Lady Bird is a sensible tribute to the spirit of Claudia Alta Taylor Johnson. . .The film's conflicts are surprisingly touching.
reviews.author: Armond White

reviews.text: Lady Bird is, instead, episodic and rambling, a ruminative look back at a crucial, defining period in its creator's life.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: Gerwig understands the pains and the humorous discomforts of growing up so acutely that Lady Bird feels like it was made just for you.
reviews.author: Oliver Whitney

reviews.text: Witty and wise, hopeful and heartbreaking.
reviews.author: Jason Bailey

reviews.text: There's an easy yet unnerving authenticity in Lady Bird, making it feel like a welcoming yet soul-baring memoir.
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: A finely wrought, deeply felt mash note to Gerwig's hometown of Sacramento, and the rare film about teenage life that puts equal weight on the dark, sad and tough parts, as it does on the joyous, raucous, euphoric moments.
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: It hit me unexpectedly-like a snowball between the eyes.
reviews.author: Rex Reed

reviews.text: Lady Bird is a masterpiece. Affecting, emotional, funny, painful. It'll make you feel things and transport you to a time you thought you'd gotten over.
reviews.author: Kristen Lopez

reviews.text: The movie is best when it undercuts its own seriousness, as when Lady Bird proclaims, "I want to be the best version of who I can be," and then follows up with, "What if this is the best version?"
reviews.author: Peter Rainer

reviews.text: It isn't every day you see a film so attuned to the outsized drama of adolescent life. The film is bursting with life and rich in observations both large and small. Kudos to Gerwig and all of her collaborators
reviews.author: Leonard Maltin

reviews.text: Greta Gerwig, the accomplished actress and writer, crafts a suburban coming-of-age story in "Lady Bird," her directorial debut...
reviews.author: Robert Levin

reviews.text: [Gerwig's] first solo flight as a director and writer is beautifully confident in its rhythm and mood, the script whip-sawing from humor to earnest emotion to raw pain and back.
reviews.author: Sheila O'Malley

reviews.text: Lady Bird isn't just the sort of film that makes any day better, but it suggests that Gerwig has a cinematic voice unlike any other, and that, even at 23, Ronan really has what it takes to blossom into one of the finest actresses of her generation.
reviews.author: Gregory Wakeman

reviews.text: There's little that's particularly unique about Ronan's title character or her various relatives, friends and lovers, but a vibrant realism makes them and everything about this movie remarkable - and kind of exhilarating.
reviews.author: Bob Strauss

reviews.text: Lady Bird finds fresh purchase in well-trodden territory by observing the human carnival from a girl's point of view.
reviews.author: Dana Stevens

reviews.text: Most memorably, in a movie that's memorable in just about every regard, there's a compact sex scene that illuminates a whole interior world of desire and values.
reviews.author: Kurt Loder

reviews.text: It may be about the selfishness and growing pains of its confused and embattled heroine, but it's made from the perspective of an artist who sees the world more clearly now than she did then.
reviews.author: Scott Tobias

reviews.text: It's funny, lively, and then devastating when it needs to be, made with the kind of confidence even its heroine could only dream of.
reviews.author: David Sims

reviews.text: Left to her own devices, Gerwig has arrived and solidified her place as one of the most invigorating, observant and authentic voices in movies today with a director's acumen to match.
reviews.author: Lindsey Bahr

reviews.text: ... Gerwig is by far one of the most talented filmmakers working today, both onscreen and behind the camera, confident and winsome in a way nearly unparalleled by her contemporaries.
reviews.author: Alissa Wilkinson

reviews.text: The poignancy of Lady Bird can be traced, yes, to its honest portrayal of growing up.
reviews.author: Bridget Read

reviews.text: ... the dialogue in "Lady Bird" is consistently and honestly funny and cliché-free.
reviews.author: John Anderson

reviews.text: One of the better solo directing debuts by an actor in recent memory.
reviews.author: Susan Wloszczyna

reviews.text: The loosely autobiographical Lady Bird is actress-writer Greta Gerwig's solo directorial debut, and it feels like the fullest realization so far of her already-patented brand of gangly bittersweet whimsy.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: It turns out that Lady Bird is the mother's coming-of-age too, and no maternal dynamic could be more refreshing in cinema.
reviews.author: Caroline Cao

reviews.text: Lady Bird is both generous and joyous, but when it stings, it stings deep.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: Unlike the rest of us, Greta Gerwig had a high-school senior year that makes a picture-perfect debut as a writer-director.
reviews.author: Harry Haun

reviews.text: Greta Gerwig is spreading her wings as a filmmaker - and she soars with "Lady Bird."
reviews.author: Amy Rowe

reviews.text: As warm as it is smart - and it is very smart - "Lady Bird" marks actor/screenwriter Greta Gerwig's superb debut as a solo director and yet another astonishing performance by star Saoirse Ronan.
reviews.author: Kenneth Turan

reviews.text: Once you've seen it-even while you're watching it, with a grin stuck on your face-you want to give thanks for how wonderful it is, how wise and funny and full of grace.
reviews.author: Joe Morgenstern

reviews.text: One of the best films of the year. In telling her own coming of age story, Gerwig proves herself a blazing talent and Ronan and Metcalf should have Oscar calling. Totally irresistible.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: Gerwig and Ronan make their heroine as finely tuned as an antenna, always quivering with signals about the new selves she might momentarily try on.
reviews.author: Stuart Klawans

reviews.text: Greta Gerwig's sweetheart of a coming of age movie is warm, witty and pretty darn wonderful.
reviews.author: Joanna Langfield

reviews.text: An affecting encapsulation of the joys, sorrows and narrow-mindedness of youth, painted with brush-strokes both harsh and tender.
reviews.author: Siddhant Adlakha

reviews.text: Perfectly exemplifies Gerwig's filmmaking voice, even if it's her fist film as director.
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: If you pay the right kind of attention to "Lady Bird" - absorbing its riffs and digressions as well as its melodies, its choral passages along with its solos and duets - you will almost certainly love it. It's hard not to.
reviews.author: A.O. Scott

reviews.text: [Saorise] Ronan's accent is American, but there's Irish in her rhythms, in the way she drives her lines home and turns every full stop into an ellipsis, a fierce demand for more.
reviews.author: David Edelstein

reviews.text: Lady Bird is an angsty coming-of-age tale set in 2002 that feels remarkably and delightfully fresh.
reviews.author: Mara Reinstein

reviews.text: Lady Bird is a perfect coming-of-age comedy for anyone who's ever had teenage wanderlust, fought with their parents, fostered a love-hate tension with their hometown or popped Communion wafers in secret.
reviews.author: Brian Truitt

reviews.text: [Lady Bird] is a shrewd, warm, witty coming-of-age movie.
reviews.author: Melissa Anderson

reviews.text: As writer and director, Greta Gerwig infuses this comedic coming-of-age drama with verbal virtuosity, gestural idiosyncrasy, and emotional vitality.
reviews.author: Richard Brody

reviews.text: In Greta Gerwig's directorial debut she's landed on something great, a film that takes on something we've all seen before but in such a complex way that it feels entirely new again.
reviews.author: Ryan Morris

reviews.text: Gerwig's directorial debut is a joy from start to finish, a warm, generous snapshot of teenage vulnerability and exuberance.
reviews.author: Lara Zarum

reviews.text: While there's comfort in the tropes we've come to recognize, what makes Lady Bird special are the touches that are uniquely Gerwig's.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: Gerwig's film feels like a memoir about the end of adolescence, each and every scene seeming to hint at an important moment that might have happened in her life.
reviews.author: Jordan Ruimy

reviews.text: There's an eccentric individualism to [Greta] Gerwig's nimble approach to form and flow of dialogue.
reviews.author: Caroline Madden

reviews.text: Lady Bird is the rare teen movie that vindicates the world's exasperating moms.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: An absolute delight.
reviews.author: Mike Ryan

reviews.text: A film of tenderness and wit, Lady Bird astutely captures the nature of the internecine warfare that habitually exists between girls in late adolescence and their mothers.
reviews.author: Graham Fuller

reviews.text: A hilarious and heartwarming experience.
reviews.author: Dwight Brown

reviews.text: It's as if Gerwig was retroactively auditioning for the school talent show, exorcising necessary demons in the process, and remembering the details with acute attention.
reviews.author: Jay Kuehner

reviews.text: Lady Bird is nothing short of tremendous, a wise film about how two people deal with ambivalence.
reviews.author: Kyle Turner

reviews.text: Vibrant and whimsical, "Lady Bird" is a hypnotic, absorbing feat, that seems destined to become a classic.
reviews.author: Clayton Davis

reviews.text: Gerwig proves that in addition to being a wonderful actor and screenwriter, she is also emerging as one of the sharpest cinematic voices of her generation.
reviews.author: David Crow

reviews.text: A uniquely American comedy, Greta Gerwig's Lady Bird is testy, humane, and firmly rooted in its time and place.
reviews.author: Christopher Gray

reviews.text: [It jumps] to the head of the class of teen comedies ... This movie has moxie.
reviews.author: Kent Turner

reviews.text: A miserabilist story about the horror of adolescence that is obviously helmed by a first-timer, Lady Bird is redeemed by a cast so sterling that I actually wished the film were longer. It's that kind of movie.
reviews.author: Walter Chaw

reviews.text: [Greta] Gerwig deftly compresses her story into montage-like bursts of narrative that never seem superficially stylish, but convey novelistic depths of emotional detail.
reviews.author: Brian D. Johnson

reviews.text: Gerwig has proven that she's equally adept behind the camera, allowing her personal experiences to inform this upbeat, charming coming-of-age comedy.
reviews.author: Tina Hassannia

reviews.text: Alternately lively and thoughtful, Lady Bird is the work of someone looking back critically on a frantic period in her own life.
reviews.author: Norman Wilner

reviews.text: Greta Gerwig's directorial debut is something special and proves that Gerwig is not only a talent in front of the camera but behind one as well. In a sea of coming of age movies, Lady Bird stands out as a truly fantastic film.
reviews.author: Scott Menzel

reviews.text: In Lady Bird, Gerwig cares about her characters enough to treat them with respect when they deserve it and to kindly skewer them when they deserve that.
reviews.author: Sarah Kurchak

reviews.text: What a joy, then, to discover that [Greta Gerwig] is equally capable at flooding a film with twisted livewire complexity.
reviews.author: Sophie Monks Kaufman

reviews.text: A lovingly observed, pitch perfect coming-of-age comedy, Gerwig's warm, astute account of the end of adolescence is a stunning solo debut.
reviews.author: Christopher Machell

reviews.text: The obvious honesty of the director makes this seemingly ordinary anecdote become something close to the spectator. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Oscar Uriel

reviews.text: Refreshingly honest, funny, and sharp.
reviews.author: Matt Goldberg

reviews.text: Lady Bird is one of the greatest debuts in recent years, and it marks an incredibly auspicious start to Gerwig's potential career behind the camera.
reviews.author: Tomas Trussow

reviews.text: There's no messing around here, Gerwig is a terrific talent on screen and on the page, and now we've got proof that as a director she's taken it up to a whole other notch.
reviews.author: Jason Gorber

reviews.text: There are no fireworks or twists or unnecessary frills here, nor should there be - this is simply perfect filmmaking from a voice that demands to be heard.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: Lady Bird will surely go down as one of the year's best films, but Greta Gerwig's feature is also a contender for having some of the strongest insightabout the winding path of adolescence this decade.
reviews.author: Christopher Schobert

reviews.text: Lady Bird is something truly special: a coming-of-age comedy so funny, perceptive, and truthful that it makes most other films about adolescence look like little more than lessons in cliché.
reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: Lady Bird is a film bursting with warmth, wit and melancholy that manages to seem fresh and unexpected despite the overly stacked nature of the subgenre.
reviews.author: Benjamin Lee

reviews.text: This is a resoundingly modern, assuredly female-voiced comedy that portends more great things to come from Gerwig behind the camera.
reviews.author: Sara Stewart

reviews.text: Exuding sunny optimism, sassy wit and sheer joie de vivre, Lady Bird could be the perfect antidote to these angst-ridden times.
reviews.author: Allan Hunter

reviews.text: Snappy, spirited and shot through with the pangs and pleasures of leaving childhood behind, Lady Bird is a sharp-witted solo first feature by actress and now writer-director Greta Gerwig.
reviews.author: Todd McCarthy

reviews.text: "Lady Bird" consolidates the style and sensibility of a generation caught between the last gasp of the 20th century and post-9/11 disillusionment like nothing else before.
reviews.author: Eric Kohn

reviews.text: The kind of modest, miraculous low-budget gem that takes on a life of its own.
reviews.author: Peter Debruge

reviews.text: This is a coming of age storyline that you've seen in one form or another for decades. It takes a truly unique voice to make yet another one worth watching. Ladies and gentleman please welcome to the stage Greta Gerwig and "Lady Bird."
reviews.author: Gregory Ellwood

reviews.text: A sweet, deeply personal portrayal of female adolescence that's more attuned to the bonds between best girlfriends than casual flings with boys, writer-director Greta Gerwig's beautiful Lady Bird flutters with the attractively loose rhythms of youth.
reviews.author: Tomris Laffly

synopsis: A teenager (Saoirse Ronan) navigates a loving but turbulent relationship with her strong-willed mother (Laurie Metcalf) over the course of an eventful and poignant senior year of high school.
